title: Subquadratic deterministic simulation of nondeterministic space
formal: For every space-constructible function \(s:\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}\) with \(s(n)\ge \lceil \log _{2}(n+2)\rceil\), is every language in \(\mathrm{NSPACE}(O(s(n)))\) decidable deterministically in \(o(s(n)^{2})\) space? Equivalently, for each such s and each language L accepted by an \(O(s(n))\)-space nondeterministic machine, must there exist one deterministic decider D for L whose maximum workspace \(g_{D}(n)\) on n-bit inputs satisfies \(\lim (n\to \infty ) g_{D}(n)/s(n)^{2}=0\)?
why: Would improve the general memory overhead for eliminating nondeterminism beyond a theorem that has stood since 1970. Even a slowly vanishing improvement would sharpen a basic relationship between deterministic and nondeterministic computation, including the logarithmic-space regime.
status_note: Full source question read and standard space conventions made explicit. Subsequent-work searches through 11 September 2026 located no unconditional resolution of the displayed general containment. Related 2025 conditional results and 2026 catalytic-memory results were checked at abstract level; full proofs were not audited.

progress.text: Savitch proves the quadratic-space simulation; the original theorem is cited and restated in the 2025 source. The 1970 article was not independently retrieved for this review.
Cook and Mertz improve tree evaluation to \(O(\log  N\cdot \log  \log  N)\) space. This is the related theorem cited by the subsequent seminar question.
Mertz asks for the general containment \(\mathrm{NSPACE}[s]\subseteq \mathrm{SPACE}[o(s^{2})]\).
The separate connectivity work reports conditional and disjunctive consequences involving Savitch-type improvements.
Edenhofer’s preprint gives a directed-reachability trade-off with additional catalytic memory. Its abstract does not give the target ordinary-space simulation.

sentences: Savitch’s theorem simulates nondeterministic space s with deterministic space \(O(s^{2})\).
This card asks whether every at-least-logarithmic space-constructible bound admits an improvement to \(o(s^{2})\).
The machine is deterministic and all ordinary working memory is charged, with no restriction on running time.
A constant-factor improvement does not suffice, while no fixed polynomial saving is required.
A resolution would sharpen the general memory cost of eliminating nondeterminism, including for logarithmic-space computation.

upgraded_from.title: Improving SPACE versus NSPACE via Tree Evaluation

definitions: Inputs are binary strings of length n. Machines have a finite control, a two-way read-only input tape and a fixed finite number of initially blank work tapes over a fixed finite alphabet. Space is the maximum total number of visited work-tape cells; the read-only input itself is not charged. Machines are uniform, with no advice, random bits, oracle or uncharged auxiliary memory. Nondeterministic machines have finitely many possible next moves, accept exactly when some branch accepts, and halt on every branch; the space bound applies to every branch and every input of length n. \(\mathrm{NSPACE}(O(s(n)))\) denotes languages with such a machine using at most \(C s(n)\) cells for some fixed C and all sufficiently large n. A deterministic decider must halt on every input, with no imposed running-time bound. A function s is space-constructible here if a deterministic machine on \(1^{n}\) can output \(1^{s}(n)\) using \(O(s(n))\) work cells, with output written on a separate write-only tape. The standard at-least-logarithmic space-constructible regime of Savitch’s theorem supplies the source’s implicit parameter convention. The little-o containment means that the decider and its improvement rate may depend on L and s. It does not require a fixed exponent saving \(s^{2- \varepsilon}\) or one common improvement rate for all languages.
answer_criterion: Prove the displayed containment for every admitted space bound and every nondeterministic language, with deterministic workspace little-o of \(s(n)^{2}\). Alternatively, refute it by identifying an admitted s and a language in \(\mathrm{NSPACE}(O(s(n)))\) for which no deterministic decider has that little-o space bound. A constant-factor saving in \(s(n)^{2}, a\) simulation of only a special graph family, or a bound that excludes separately supplied catalytic memory does not meet the stated guarantee.

context_blocks.title: What nondeterminism costs in memory
context_blocks.text: A nondeterministic machine can choose among several next moves and accepts if some sequence of choices succeeds. A deterministic simulation must decide the same question without those choices. Savitch’s theorem shows that squaring the workspace is enough, even though the simulation may take much longer.

context_blocks.title: Any vanishing fraction would count
context_blocks.text: If a nondeterministic computation uses about s cells, the target is a deterministic simulation whose memory divided by \(s^{2}\) tends to zero. A bound such as \(s^{2}/\log (s+2)\) would qualify, while \(0.01s^{2}\) would not. These expressions illustrate the meaning of little-o; the question imposes no particular rate of improvement.

context_blocks.title: The logarithmic-space case
context_blocks.text: For \(s(n)\) of order log n, the target becomes deterministic \(o(\log ^{2} n)\) space for every language in nondeterministic logarithmic space. This includes directed reachability: given a directed graph and two vertices, decide whether there is a directed path between them. The full card quantifies over all admitted s and does not restrict inputs to a special graph family.

context_blocks.title: Where tree evaluation fits in the history
context_blocks.text: The source was posed after Cook and Mertz’s STOC 2024 improvement for tree evaluation. That problem evaluates a tree of explicitly supplied functions and leaf values, and its stated space bound is \(O(\log  N\cdot \log  \log  N)\) in the tree-evaluation input size N. The general nondeterministic-space simulation remains the target of the 2025 question.

context_blocks.title: Conditional progress
context_blocks.text: The 2025 connectivity paper states alternatives linking improvements in reachability and derandomization. Its abstract does not give an unconditional simulation of every nondeterministic-space computation in \(o(s^{2})\) space.

context_blocks.title: Catalytic memory is an additional resource
context_blocks.text: A 2026 directed-reachability preprint trades ordinary workspace against catalytic memory, which begins with arbitrary contents and must be restored. Its abstract does not state the requested improvement in total ordinary workspace.
